To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
technology use during sleep was related to poor sleep quality, which in turn was associated with depression and anxiety.

(1) technology use during sleep is associated with poor sleep, (2) poor sleep is associated with symptoms of depression and anxiety, (3) technology use during the night is related to poor sleep, and (4) poor sleep mediates the relationship between technology use during the evening and symptoms of depression and/or anxiety.
technology-related sleep disturbances are linked with poor mental health outcomes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of technology-related sleep disruption on psychological health, specifically depression and anxiety.
how technology use after the start of sleep is related to sleep quality and how sleep quality is related to depression and anxiety.
the relationship among technology use during the nighttime hours, sleep quality, depression, and anxiety.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of technology at night can lead to sleep disturbances, which in turn can lead to depression and anxiety in college students.
technology use after sleep time is associated with poorer sleep quality and that sleep quality is a partial mediator between technology use and depression and anxiety symptoms.
technology use after the start of sleep time is related to sleep quality and sleep quality is a significant mediator between technology use and symptoms of depression/anxiousness.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
students who have trouble sleeping are more likely to be depressed and anxious and that technology use is associated with sleep quality.
the use of technology after the onset of the night's sleep is associated with poor sleep quality and that this poor sleep quality is related to symptoms of depression and anxiety.
technology use after the start of sleep can have negative effects on sleep and that these effects can lead to depression and anxiety.
The main takeaway from our work is that
college students are using technology during sleep, which may be contributing to poor sleep quality.
college students are not sleeping enough and are spending more time awake in bed due to technology use than previously thought.
students should be encouraged to set limits around the use of technology after the onset of bedtime.
